chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Bebop in the air, Monk and San Juan Hill
summary: Danny says bebop ideas were in the air, Monk patterned on Profit, and Edgar Sampson took Stompin' at the Savoy from Profit. End of Tape 2 side B.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: What Charlie out in the West?

He came from Kansas City and Dizzy's from South Carolina. Well, that bug was in the air, and they got the nucleus of this thing, see. And Thelonious was patterning...kind of patterning his playing after Clarence Profit. Because Clarence Profit and all them come off that San Juan Hill. You know, Monk lived down there on 99th Street [sic: 63rd Street].
The Jungle, they used to call it.
Yeah, the Jungle. All of them come out that Jungle, see. Partly West Indian and partly Carolinas.

Yeah, all of them, Gene Michaels(?) and all of them before they come to Harlem. And that's the basics of the thing. So when the Bebop come in, it didn't make too much of a thing with me. You know? I'm not being different. Because I'd heard Clarence Profit makin' them progressions. Because Edgar Sampson had taken "Stompin' at The Savoy" from Clarence Profit. But Clarence Profit was a little cat, didn't say nothin'.

Yeah, that was Clarence Profit's idea, that composition. Mark that down. When you see Jimmy Sherman, ask him where can you get Clarence Profit's records. He must have made about a couple of dozen records. Fantastic piano player.
